#### Initial Plot of Data {#sec-pmd-643}

[**Plot of Data**]{#sec-pmd-643-plot}

The first step in fitting a nonlinear function is to simply plot the data.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false
#| label: fig-pmd-643-data
#| fig-cap: "Coefficient of thermal expansion versus temperature"
hahn <- read_table(
  here::here("datasets", "HAHN1.DAT"),
  skip = 25,
  col_names = c("temperature", "thermal_expansion")
)

ggplot(hahn, aes(temperature, thermal_expansion)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Temperature (K)", y = "Coefficient of Thermal Expansion") +
  theme_light()
```

This plot initially shows a fairly steep slope that levels off to a more gradual slope. This type of curve can often be modeled with a rational function model. The plot also indicates that there do not appear to be any outliers in this data.
